answer: At the XL scale, H-Net (space), H-Net (1-stage), and H-Net (2-stage) cross over the tokenized Transformer after 200B, 100B, and 30B training bytes, respectively [Dynamic Chunking for End-to-End Hierarchical Sequence Modeling, arXiv:2507.07955v2, PDF p. 12, §3.1 Language Modeling]. Beyond these crossover points, the performance advantage of the H-Net methods widens progressively [Dynamic Chunking for End-to-End Hierarchical Sequence Modeling, arXiv:2507.07955v2, PDF p. 12, §3.1 Language Modeling].
question: At the XL scale, the byte-level H-Nets start behind the tokenized Transformer. After how many training bytes does each one cross over, and what happens to the gap after that?
raw_answer: At the XL scale, H-Net (space), H-Net (1-stage), and H-Net (2-stage) cross over the tokenized Transformer after 200B, 100B, and 30B training bytes, respectively [[cite:e9249953b98782f7]]. Beyond these crossover points, the performance advantage of the H-Net methods widens progressively [[cite:e9249953b98782f7]].
